Are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

Recent findings suggest that what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

According to recent reports, one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

If you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

Industry observers note that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

Recent findings suggest that how do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

Industry observers note that if you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

According to recent reports, you could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Sources indicate that plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Industry observers note that of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

HealthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

Sources indicate that the more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator reveals potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

It has been revealed that if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

According to recent reports, nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Recent findings suggest that plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Industry observers note that do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

Either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Latest York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

The Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

How much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com indicates a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Industry observers note that investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

But what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

According to recent reports, since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

According to recent reports, housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

According to recent reports, that remarked, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

If you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

For example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

Sources indicate that you can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

Real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

You can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Industry observers note that fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

Recent findings suggest that while returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

It has been revealed that you can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal plans start at $3 per month, while a family initiative costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Industry observers note that projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

The best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Industry observers note that earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

In a recent development, that said, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

According to recent reports, how much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

That remarked, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

If you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, enhancement a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

Industry observers note that if you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

In a recent development, another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

Industry observers note that finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

According to recent reports, you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

Finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

According to recent reports, there you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

Keep Savings in the Bank During a Recession – Cash at Home Is Barely Insured

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leave your savings in the bank when a recession looms, and keep your balance at each bank under the $250,000 insurance limit.
  • In a recent development, bank failures do rise in a recession, which is why pulling your savings out can feel like the careful move.
  • According to recent reports, the FDIC, the federal agency that insures bank deposits, notes no depositor has lost insured money since it was founded in 1933.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leave your savings in the bank when a recession looms, and keep your balance at each bank under the $250,000 insurance limit. Insured deposits have been paid in full through every downturn, while cash at home can be stolen or burned and gets only $200 of coverage under a typical homeowners policy.

In a recent development, bank failures do rise in a recession, which is why pulling your savings out can feel like the careful move. It actually takes money out of a federally insured account and leaves it where almost nothing protects it.

According to recent reports, the FDIC, the federal agency that insures bank deposits, notes no depositor has lost insured money since it was founded in 1933. That record held through the last major wave, when 465 banks failed from 2008 through 2012, by the FDIC’s count. Federally insured credit unions have similar coverage through the National Credit Union Administration, and none of their members has lost a cent of insured savings either.

Industry observers note that cash at home has no such backing. A burglar or a house fire can take all of it, and it earns nothing while inflation shrinks what it buys. The FDIC’s disaster guide suggests depositing large sums at an insured bank and holding a small amount of cash for food and supplies, since ATMs and credit cards may not work in a disaster.

Say a family withdraws $20,000 in a panic and hides it in a closet. If a fire or a break-in takes it, a typical homeowners policy covers only $200 of cash, according to the nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook, so at least $19,800 is gone. Kept in an insured savings account paying 3.5% a year, the same $20,000 would be covered in full and earn $700 in its first year.

Recent findings suggest that hold your emergency fund, sized to your bare-bones bills, in an insured high-yield savings account. FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per bank, for each ownership category, meaning how you own the account, such as alone or jointly.

Total your balances at each bank before you move a dollar, and send only the amount over the limit to an account at a second insured bank.

Compare the best high-yield savings accounts for an insured place to keep your savings.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that quit smoking or vaping and you stop spending on packs or pods, often thousands of dollars a year, and later pay less for life and health insurance.
  • A pack a day costs your local pack price times 365, and vaping costs a week’s pods or e-liquid times 52.
  • Recent findings suggest that take a pack-a-day smoker whose proposal covers the patches they quit with.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that quit smoking or vaping and you stop spending on packs or pods, often thousands of dollars a year, and later pay less for life and health insurance. Most health plans must cover quit-smoking counseling and medication at no cost, so ask your doctor to prescribe nicotine patches, and call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free coaching.

Work out your own yearly cost. A pack a day costs your local pack price times 365, and vaping costs a week’s pods or e-liquid times 52.

Recent findings suggest that take a pack-a-day smoker whose proposal covers the patches they quit with. At $9 a pack, they keep about $3,300 in the first year, before any insurance savings. Most life insurers charge nicotine users, vapers included, higher premiums than nonsmokers pay for equal coverage. Insurers selling plans on HealthCare.gov and state marketplaces can add up to 50% to a tobacco user’s premium.

Smoke also counts against a car or a house when you sell it. Its odor can be hard and expensive to clean out of a car. A 2008 San Diego State University study found nonsmokers asked 7% to 9% more for their used cars than smokers did for comparable ones. In a Drexel University survey, 96% of Philadelphia-area realtors stated a house where people smoke is harder to sell.

Recent findings suggest that under federal guidance, a job-based or marketplace plan complies by covering at least two quit attempts a year at no cost. Each attempt includes four counseling sessions and 90 days of FDA-approved medication, from nicotine patches and gum to prescription pills.

Industry observers note that that coverage includes over-the-counter patches and gum only with a prescription, so ask your doctor for one instead of buying them off the shelf. Then call 1-800-QUIT-NOW, which connects you to your state’s free quitline. Its coaches help vapers too, and some state quitlines give callers free medication.

In a recent development, the insurance savings take longer. For marketplace plans, tobacco use means regular use in the past six months, so once you’ve gone six months without tobacco, you can answer no to the tobacco question on your next application and drop the surcharge. Most life insurers want 12 months without nicotine before they’ll rate you a nonsmoker, and patches and gum count as nicotine.

So write down the day you stop all nicotine, and a year later, ask your life insurer to reprice your policy at nonsmoker rates.

The Investments That Hold Up in a Recession – Own Them Before It Hits

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (615 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury bonds, cash, and the steadiest stocks have held up best in past recessions, but they protected only the investors who already owned them.
  • That switch gets the timing backward.
  • The 2008 crash demonstrates the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury bonds, cash, and the steadiest stocks have held up best in past recessions, but they protected only the investors who already owned them. Choose your stock and bond mix and set aside emergency cash while the economy is growing, then rebalance through the slump instead of selling stocks for safety once the news turns bad.

That switch gets the timing backward. By the time a recession is in the news, you’d be selling stocks after they’ve fallen and buying safe havens after other investors have already pushed their prices up.

The 2008 crash demonstrates the cost. That year the S&P 500 lost 37% while 10-year Treasury bonds gained 20%, according to yearly returns compiled by NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran. The National Bureau of Economic Research, which determines when U.S. recessions start and end, didn’t announce that one until Dec. 1, 2008, about a year after it began. An investor who moved from stocks to Treasury bonds at the end of that year then lost 11% on the bonds in 2009, while the S&P 500 gained 26%.

Which haven protects you depends on what drives the downturn. In a crash that sends investors looking for safety and pulls interest rates down, as in 2008 and 2020, high-quality bonds gain while stocks fall. In a drop driven by inflation, as in 2022, rising rates cut the value of bonds already issued, so bonds fall along with stocks. Consumer prices rose 6.5% that year, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports.

Here’s how each haven did in 2008 and 2020, and where it let investors down:.

The bonds have to be high quality. Corporate bonds with a middling credit rating, Baa, lost 3% in 2008, the year 10-year Treasury bonds gained 20%.

You can’t tell in advance which kind of downturn is coming, so a mix built for a recession holds both high-quality bonds and cash.

Some ideas pitched as recession-proof rarely belong in an ordinary investor’s mix.

Pick a split between stocks and high-quality bonds that you’d stick with if stocks fell 37%, as they did in 2008. Then write your investing rules down, including that split and the date you’ll check it. Keep an emergency fund that covers your bare-bones bills in cash outside the mix, so a layoff doesn’t force you to sell stocks at a low. Money you’ll need within a few years belongs in safe places that earn interest instead.

Rebalancing your portfolio through the slump means selling some of what held up to buy more of what fell. Take $100,000 split 60% in stocks tracking the S&P 500 and 40% in 10-year Treasury bonds at the start of 2008, with Damodaran’s yearly returns and no fees or taxes. Three moves at the end of 2008 led to different results by the end of 2009:.

Decide now how far your mix can drift before you rebalance, such as 5 percentage points from your target share in stocks. Then in the next slump, selling what held up to buy what fell is a rule you already wrote, not a call you make in a panic.

Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

It has been revealed that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That said, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

According to recent reports, you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

Sources indicate that no matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

Sources indicate that to save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

In a recent development, other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment aims.

Sources indicate that if you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment aims and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Industry observers note that once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

In a recent development, it’s key to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as swiftly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Recent findings suggest that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Industry observers note that having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete blueprint that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that your library’s app is usually Libby, since over 90% of North American public libraries use OverDrive, which makes it. Sign in with your library card to read on a phone, tablet, or Kobo e-reader, or to send most borrowed e-books to a Kindle if your library is in the U.S.

The catch is the wait. Publishers often let a library lend each digital copy to just one reader at a time, so popular titles have wait lists. Place holds early, and if one becomes available while you’re reading another book, suspend it to keep your place in line.

Check your library’s website for what else your card covers. If Hoopla, a second lending app, is on the list, try it whenever Libby’s wait runs long. Its Instant titles have no wait list, though your library caps how many you can borrow each month.

Sources indicate that for everything else, buy only on sale. BookBub’s free daily email lists limited-time deals at the major e-book stores, and it features a book only when it’s free or marked down by at least half. For a title you’re watching, eReaderIQ, a free tracker, emails you when its Kindle price falls to the amount you set.

Industry observers note that say you borrow through Libby, read classics free, and pay about $2 for each deal you buy. Then Kindle+, formerly Kindle Unlimited, costs $11.99 a month plus tax, about what six $2 deals cost, but it only lends its books, up to 20 at a time, while deals are yours to keep. It pays for itself at seven or more of its books a month that you’d otherwise buy, so check that its catalog carries the authors you read.

For the next e-book you want, place a Libby hold and set an eReaderIQ alert at the price you’d pay, then take whichever comes first.

Download Libby and sign in with your library card to place that first hold.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, A week before rent is due, you’re offering your landlord a initiative.
  • Recent findings suggest that an eviction costs the landlord too, in court fees and in rent that goes unpaid while the case runs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re short on rent this month, call your landlord before it’s due and offer part of it now with a firm date for the rest, then get the deal in writing. The same day, call 211 or visit 211.org to reach local emergency rental assistance and charities that can cover the gap.

In a recent development, A week before rent is due, you’re offering your landlord a initiative. A week after, you’re explaining a missed payment that may already carry a late fee.

Recent findings suggest that an eviction costs the landlord too, in court fees and in rent that goes unpaid while the case runs. Offering part of the rent now and the rest by a set date gives your landlord a cheaper way to get paid than going to court.

Recent findings suggest that say your $1,000 rent is due on the first and you have $400. Call on the 25th and offer to pay the $400 on the first and the other $600 by the 20th. Ask whether your landlord will waive the late fee as long as you keep to the blueprint, then send a text or email that restates the amounts and dates so you both have the deal in writing.

Then call 211 to find the $600. The federal rental assistance created during the pandemic ended in September 2025, so the money now comes from state and local programs, charities such as the Salvation Army and Catholic Charities, churches, and one-time emergency grants. A 211 specialist can tell you which of these serve your area. If you’re behind on other bills too, ask about emergency help with those bills on the same call.

In a recent development, skip payday loans and cash advance apps. With both, you borrow against your next paycheck, which only moves the shortfall to next month’s rent. A common payday fee of $15 per $100 borrowed works out to an annual rate of almost 400% on a two-week loan, according to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

Apply for help the same day you make the deal with your landlord. Rental assistance can take several weeks to arrive after you apply, and the rest of your rent is due on the date you promised.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some big companies pay every dollar of tuition at their partner schools, even for part-time workers starting on day one, and others pay up to a set amount each year. Before you take a job for the benefit, check which schools and degrees it covers and whether you’d owe the money back if you leave.

Chosen for that benefit, an hourly job can be a debt-free route to a degree.

The benefits come in two kinds. The most generous pay all of the tuition, though only at partner schools and usually only for programs in the firm’s catalog, and a few start the day you’re hired. The rest pay up to a set amount, often $5,250 a year, and you cover anything above it. At many of these employers, part-time workers qualify too.

Start with the catalog. A full-tuition benefit pays only at its partner schools and for the programs on its list, so find the degree you want there, and note how long you’d work before you can enroll.

Then ask whether you’d owe any of the money back if you left. Walmart and Starbucks don’t require you to stay after you finish, while McDonald’s makes managers who miss its transcript deadlines repay the money.

Recent findings suggest that last, make sure the degree pays. The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Occupational Outlook Handbook lists each job’s median pay and the education it usually takes, so look up the job you want before you pick a program. If you already owe student loans, also ask whether the employer pays toward them, a separate benefit some companies offer.

Take a part-time Walmart cashier with no college credits who earns an online bachelor’s degree from Southern Fresh Hampshire University, a Live Better U partner. Walmart’s benefit leaves her little or nothing to pay for tuition and required books. Paying her own way, she’d owe SNHU’s online rate of $354 a credit for 120 credits, or $42,480. Say she borrowed it at 6.52%, the rate Federal Student Aid set for new undergraduate loans for 2026-27, with no interest added while she’s in school. Repaid over 10 years, that’s about $483 a month, or about $15,450 in interest.

Before you accept an offer, ask the recruiter for the benefit’s written terms and its list of partner schools, then enroll in a covered program as soon as you’re eligible.

Certificates of Deposit (CDs) work similarly to online savings accounts or money market accounts in terms of offering great returns with zero risk. The difference is, CDs “lock your money up” for a specified period of time. To access your funds before the term ends, you’ll have to pay a penalty.

It has been revealed that although CDs offer less liquidity than a regular checking account or savings account, you might get a higher rate of return with this financial product. This is especially true if you open a CD account with a longer timeline; for example, a 60-month CD instead of a 12-month CD.

According to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), national average CD rates range from 0.23% to 1.81% depending on the CD term, as of writing.

Retired Man Tries to Spend More Money, Mostly Fails

📅 16 Jan 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1487 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Money Mustache lost some credibility among the faithful when he wrote this blog post about actually trying to spend a bit more money, while buying a Tesla as the first step in that program.
  • “I’m such an enlightened middle-aged Badass, adjusting habits and realigning myself at the snap of my fingers.
  • So, two years passed with an even greater feeling of abundance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A couple of years ago, Mr. Money Mustache lost some credibility among the faithful when he wrote this blog post about actually trying to spend a bit more money, while buying a Tesla as the first step in that program.

I thought to myself at the time,.

“I’m such an enlightened middle-aged Badass, adjusting habits and realigning myself at the snap of my fingers. Onward to the next forty eight years of the Good Life!”.

So, two years passed with an even greater feeling of abundance. I had a marvelous time traveling everywhere and spending money like I thought a proper wealthy person would do.

I dined out in stylish restaurants, booked hotels based on their niceness rather than their cheapness, paid extra to sit in the “reduced torture” seats of the airplanes, and gave zero fucks about paying double for groceries if I happened to be in a Whole Foods rather than my usual Sam’s Club and Costco (and yes I treat myself to memberships at both warehouse stores!).

According to recent reports, among the highlights, my son and I have worked our way though a nice selection of late night EDM concerts and three Meowwolf art venues including a Christmas Day road trip from our winter home in Tempe Arizona to Las Vegas last year. And having spent much of the year as a single man, I had a wide open schedule to just meet up with friends, explore new places and meet new people as opportunities came up. It felt like a year of adventurous transition, which means it felt like much more than twelve months.

With all this flashy spending, I was sure my budget must have crept back into full American Consumer territory. But I was having too much fun to bother adding it all up to check.

Until recently, when I was doing another round of informal coaching for a friend and we both decided to tally our spending for the past year to compare notes.

When I finally finished sorting all of those transactions into a spreadsheet and hit the “sum” button, the results surprised me.

While my overall spending had indeed increased (especially in travel-related categories), the substantial-picture effect was still pretty minimal. Depending on how I account for things like the car and my business expenses, my spending went from $20,000 to about $30,000 (plus the usual hidden subsidy of a paid-off house.).

It has been revealed that this level could still be sustained by a $1 million investment nest egg. Since my investments are quite a bit higher than that (especially after these recent years of crazy economic growth and the never-ending stock market rally), I’m still way under budget.

Although I still “failed” to really increase my spending to the MMM-recommended levels for old wealthy people, this still makes me happy, because I have genuinely had more fun with the abundance mindset, and I can keep trying more life experiments in the coming years.

As we covered in the 2019 article on the idea of an Optimization Council, it’s always a good idea to compare our spending, tips and tricks on how to get the most out of life. Almost twenty years into early retirement, this is where I have landed so far, although I’m always learning and open to feedback.

Anyway, let’s cut the wistful commentary and get into the budget.

It has been revealed that in summary: Wow, how interesting! When we compare this to my 2019 post on that year’s spending, it’s only a bit higher even after all the inflation we have seen in recent years. I spent more on travel and fun, but less on home renovation – partly because I was away so much I didn’t have as much time to work on my house. The health insurance is a new cost too since I was self-insured back then.

My budget is notably missing the biggest expense for most people, which is housing costs. This is because I paid off my house long ago, and I also love working on and taking care of my own home, which means there are no bills for lawn mowing, plumbers, tree pruning or handyman services.

This strategy is not for everyone, and it’s not even the optimum financial one for me – I would have been better off taking out the biggest mortgage I could get at 3% back in the sweet borrowing times of 2021, and putting all that principal to work in stock index funds where it would have almost doubled since then. But I still get a great peace of mind from just having no mortgage payment, and there’s really no better way to use your money than to buy such good feelings. Also, I get a secondary benefit of not having to buy house insurance, which saves me another $2000 per year, boosting my effective return on that payoff.

Recent findings suggest that first of all, the biggest money saving factor of good health and good luck has continued, meaning I’ve still had no actual medical expenses. But I still do maintain two layers of health care support which together feel very much like the ultimate version of health insurance: a membership with a top of the line Direct Primary Care (DPC) medical clinic ($107 per month) plus a high-deductible plan ($201) with a health sharing organization called Sedera.

The combined cost of $308 per month is less than the cheapest Bronze initiative in the field of standard health insurance, yet I get personalized support with zero deductible for almost all typical medical needs, plus some protection from larger medical bills if my good luck runs out.

Sources indicate that but as a disclaimer, I’m not an expert on medical needs and health insurance because I’ve had so little experience with the system. And the highest priority in my life is arranging my days for maximum health to give me the best chance of keeping it this way.

When it comes down to it, money is a tool for survival and if we’re lucky, self actualization. So I’m always asking myself if there’s anything I can change or improve to make the most of this good fortune.

I also try to keep in mind an interesting principle of happiness, which indicates that,.

Fixing your persistent problems is more effective than just doubling down on things that are already good in your life.

It has been revealed that for me, there are already a lot of good things which don’t need improving. My family, friends, relationships, health, food and daily activities are pretty much as good as I could imagine.

Sources indicate that the only annoyance I can think of is physical chaos: I have a lot of space-intensive hobbies like construction and music, and I right now live in a pretty small house which is basically maxed out. I could really use a doubling of my workshop space from the current 2-car, 440 square foot garage to maybe a thousand or so.

It has been revealed that but I also love where I live and wouldn’t want to give up my views, neighbors or current place. So I’ll keep optimizing what I’ve got unless some perfect opportunity comes up for a bigger place right on my block.

According to recent reports, in the longer run, a mountain compound with its own cliffs and stream are also on my “maybe” list. But once again, my days and life are already overbooked with joyful things. My existing house and our HQ Coworking space already have long to-do lists. Would I actually be happier if I added another place to my portfolio? So I keep this idea on the shelf until I’m willing to trade it for another existing commitment – like selling my house or the coworking space.

But for now, I’m just extremely excited to blaze into 2025 with loads abundance and piles of challenging stuff on my to-do list. And I wish you the same!

In the Comments: Where are you at on this spectrum of stinginess versus abundance mentality, and fulfilment versus longing in life?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Keeping most of your savings in a few stocks makes sense for company founders and full-time investors. For everyone else, one company’s collapse can erase years of saving. Diversify by owning thousands of stocks of every size and sector through one low-cost total-market or total-world index fund, and skip extra funds that hold the same companies.

In a recent development, enron, Lehman Brothers, and General Electric were household names, and each tech giant’s stock fell 90% or more from its high. Anyone holding little besides one of them had lost most of their savings at the low, and Enron and Lehman went bankrupt.

It has been revealed that A founder can keep a fortune in one stock because they run the firm. Warren Buffett’s case against diversifying is for experts. In a 1993 shareholder letter, he wrote that owning many stocks makes no sense for investors who understand businesses well enough to find five to 10 fairly priced companies with lasting advantages. Everyone else, he wrote, should own many stocks, such as through an index fund.

It has been revealed that finance professor Hendrik Bessembinder found that four of every seven U.S. stocks since 1926 earned less over their lifetimes than one-month Treasury bills, short-term loans to the government. The best-performing 4% of companies produced all of the market’s gain over those bills, since the rest together only matched them. A handful of stocks will probably miss that 4%, and a fund that owns the whole market holds all of it.

Diversifying protects you from one firm, industry, or country going bad, not from a falling market. The S&P 500, an index of 500 large U.S. companies, lost about 37% in 2008 including dividends.

Industry observers note that diversifying costs almost nothing. One fund, Vanguard Total World Stock ETF, holds more than 10,000 stocks in the U.S. and abroad for 0.06% a year, or $6 on every $10,000. A total-market fund covers thousands of U.S. stocks.

Choose an index fund, not an actively managed fund whose manager picks the stocks, and keep any stocks you buy on your own to a small slice of your portfolio. If your job gives you tech giant shares, cap your employer’s stock too.

The opposite mistake is owning several funds that hold the same companies. FINRA, the brokerage industry’s regulator, suggests checking whether your funds hold similar companies. Look up each fund’s 10 largest holdings on its own page, and when the same names top two lists, one total-market fund can replace both.

Buy that fund through one of the best online brokers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the cheapest ways to fly Star Alliance business and first class.

Points for Business/First Class.

Picture this: you settle into a Lufthansa Boeing 747-8 business class seat on the upper deck, somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of Champagne in hand, your fully flat bed already made up behind you. Newly introduced York to Frankfurt — a route that commands $4,000 to $8,000 in cash for a business class ticket — and you're here for 63,000 Avianca LifeMiles. No fuel surcharges. No carrier-imposed fees eating into your redemption. Just the experience. That's the moment the FI community lives for. Not the luxury itself — though Lufthansa's business class product is genuinely exceptional — but the *math*. The realization that the loyalty system has a pricing gap so wide you could fly a 747 through it. Here's what the numbers actually mean. At the low end, a $4,000 business class ticket redeemed for 63,000 points works out to **6.3 cents per point (CPP)**. At the high end — peak travel season, last-minute pricing, transatlantic demand — that same seat hits $8,000 in cash, which means your LifeMiles are delivering **12.7 cents per point**. For context, most travel rewards experts consider 1–2 CPP a baseline for points value. You're achieving 6 to 12 times that baseline. The reason this feels like a genuine inefficiency rather than just a deal: Avianca LifeMiles prices Star Alliance awards on a **fixed award chart** that doesn't fluctuate with cash fare demand. When airlines raise transatlantic business class fares during summer holidays or major events, your points cost stays exactly the same. The gap between what the market charges and what LifeMiles charges simply grows wider. And then there's the no-fuel-surcharge policy — the detail that separates LifeMiles from competitors like British Airways Avios, which can pile $600+ in carrier surcharges onto a single redemption. With LifeMiles, you pay government taxes only, typically $50–$150 for a transatlantic itinerary. That's it. For the ChooseFI community, this redemption represents exactly the kind of asymmetric value that underpins a great travel rewards strategy: use points where cash prices are highest, eliminate fees wherever possible, and fly a product you'd never justify paying full price for — because you didn't have to.

The core insight here is understanding why Avianca LifeMiles prices Star Alliance awards so aggressively — and then understanding how to get points into the program quickly enough to actually use them.

It has been revealed that avianca is a Star Alliance member, which means it has reciprocal award booking agreements with every other Star Alliance carrier — United, Lufthansa, Swiss, ANA, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, and more. Like all alliance programs, LifeMiles can sell award seats on partner airlines. The pricing is set by Avianca's own award chart, not by Lufthansa's chart or United's chart.

This is the pricing inefficiency. Lufthansa's own frequent flyer program (Miles & More) charges over 100,000 miles for the same transatlantic business class route and layers on fuel surcharges. United MileagePlus charges 70,000–88,000 miles for the same seat. Avianca LifeMiles charges 63,000 miles with zero carrier surcharges. Same seat. Same plane. Wildly different cost.

Sources indicate that avianca keeps rates competitive because they want their program to be attractive to non-Avianca flyers — it's a revenue play. And because their route network is South America-focused, they've built a powerful award program that earns loyalty from customers who may never set foot on an Avianca plane.

Many programs claim no surcharges, then quietly pass through "carrier-imposed fees" that look indistinguishable from surcharges. LifeMiles is one of the genuine exceptions. On partner award bookings — including Lufthansa, Swiss, and other carriers that traditionally levy heavy surcharges — LifeMiles charges only government taxes. For a JFK–FRA business class award, expect to pay roughly $50–$150 out of pocket. That's the full cash outlay.

According to recent reports, this is where the transfer partner ecosystem matters. LifeMiles accepts transfers from:.

Recent findings suggest that the instant Citi transfer is particularly powerful: if you find available award space today, you can move points and call LifeMiles to book within the same session. Capital One and Bilt are nearly as fast. Marriott's 3:1 ratio makes it less efficient unless you have a large Bonvoy balance and no better option.

According to recent reports, lifeMiles runs frequent purchased miles sales, often 100%+ bonus miles on purchases. This is a legitimate strategy for topping off your balance when you're a few thousand miles short of a redemption. Combined with transfer partners, it creates significant flexibility. Watch for promotions at lifemiles.com — they typically appear 6–8 times per year.

The golden rule of any points transfer: never transfer miles until you've confirmed award availability. LifeMiles miles are non-refundable once transferred, and award space can disappear in hours.

Recent findings suggest that united MileagePlus has one of the best Star Alliance partner award search tools available to the public. Go to united.com, start a search as if you're booking an award ticket, and look for business class availability on Lufthansa or Swiss flights on your target route. United displays Lufthansa partner space accurately in most cases. You're looking for "saver" level availability — marked as "X" class on Lufthansa.

Lufthansa's own website (lufthansa.com) sometimes indicates availability that United misses, and vice versa. Search both. You're not booking here — just confirming the seat exists.

According to recent reports, an ExpertFlyer subscription ($10/month) lets you set availability alerts for specific routes and dates. For a high-value redemption like this, it's often worth one month of the service to monitor your target window.

Recent findings suggest that lifeMiles opens its booking window 355 days in advance. For peak travel periods — summer transatlantic, major European events — set a calendar reminder to search at the 355-day mark. Business class award space on Lufthansa releases in small batches and fills quickly.

Transfer exactly what you need — 63,000 miles for a one-way business class transatlantic award — plus a small buffer of 2,000–3,000 miles for potential routing variations.

According to recent reports, go to lifemiles.com and search your award. The website has improved but can still be inconsistent with partner availability display. If the online search doesn't show the space you found on United.com, call LifeMiles directly at their customer service line. Have your flight numbers, dates, and cabin class ready. Phone agents can access and book partner availability that the website sometimes fails to display.

In a recent development, after booking, you'll receive a confirmation email with a PNR (record locator). Verify this on the operating carrier's website — go to lufthansa.com or swiss.com and look up your reservation using the PNR. If it pulls up correctly, your booking is solid. Save this confirmation and check it once more 72 hours before departure.

It has been revealed that avianca LifeMiles uses a distance-based award chart for Star Alliance partner flights, and their chart is consistently 15-40% cheaper than competing programs for the same seats. The reason is strategic: Avianca wants to attract members to its loyalty program, and aggressive pricing on aspirational redemptions is how they compete with larger alliances. For you, this means the exact same Lufthansa First Class seat or ANA business class seat costs significantly fewer points when booked through LifeMiles versus through United MileagePlus or the carrier directly. The catch is that LifeMiles availability depends on the operating carrier releasing award space to partners, so you still need to search on the carrier or United.com before transferring.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shop for Instacart if you know your local stores and want daytime or weekend hours you pick, since each batch demonstrates its pay and expected tip before you accept. Take only batches whose pay and tip clearly cover the drive’s cost, because a small tip on a long drive leaves you little once gas and car wear come out.

Instacart’s sign-up page offers one role, the full-service shopper, an independent contractor who shops for and delivers batches of up to four orders. The 20,538 shoppers who tracked their pay with Gridwise made a median $12.21 an hour of active time in 2025, 42% of it tips, before self-employment tax and car costs of 76 cents a mile at the IRS’s business rate.

Sources indicate that instacart suits careful shoppers who know their local stores and want daytime or weekend hours they set, since quick, well-tipped batches pay the most per hour. Drivers in a busy restaurant market who’d rather not shop can deliver takeout for DoorDash instead.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Online stores reprice items as demand, stock, and rivals’ prices change, and some also use your location or browsing history to set the price you see.
  • From one screen, you can’t tell whether a price jumped for every shopper or just for you.
  • In 2012, The Wall Street Journal found Staples’ website showing one shopper a stapler for $15.79 and another, a few miles away, the same stapler for $14.29.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Online stores reprice items as demand, stock, and rivals’ prices change, and some also use your location or browsing history to set the price you see. Before you buy, check the item at another store and in a logged-out private window, then set a price alert instead of guessing when the price will drop.

From one screen, you can’t tell whether a price jumped for every shopper or just for you. Both happen, and the second has been documented for over a decade.

In 2012, The Wall Street Journal found Staples’ website showing one shopper a stapler for $15.79 and another, a few miles away, the same stapler for $14.29. The lower price usually went to shoppers the site judged to be within about 20 miles of an OfficeMax or Office Depot store. In January 2025, the Federal Trade Commission published first findings from its study of the firms retailers hire to set prices. Details like your precise location or browsing history can often be used to give you a different price than other shoppers get for the same goods, the agency found.

Industry observers note that in New York, the Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act requires a store that sets a price from your personal data to say so with the notice “This price was set by an algorithm using your personal data.” Since Oct. 1, 2026, a Maryland law has barred large grocers and grocery delivery services from using personal data to charge shoppers more for groceries.

Before you pay, run three checks:.

A price alert beats refreshing the page, since you can’t predict when software working from data you never see will cut the price. Google Shopping’s price tracking emails you when the price drops below a target you choose, so base that target on the item’s price history.

Set up your first price alert on Google Shopping.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The cheaper bag of pet food isn’t always the cheaper one to feed.
  • In a recent development, the price per pound on a shelf tag misses how long each pound lasts.
  • According to recent reports, take two 30-pound bags for a 50-pound dog, at illustrative prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The cheaper bag of pet food isn’t always the cheaper one to feed. A denser food holds more calories in each cup, so your pet eats less of it and the bag lasts longer. Before you buy or switch, divide each bag’s price by the days it lasts at your pet’s feeding amount.

In a recent development, the price per pound on a shelf tag misses how long each pound lasts. A pound of a calorie-dense food feeds your pet for more days than a pound of a less dense one.

According to recent reports, take two 30-pound bags for a 50-pound dog, at illustrative prices. One costs $45 and lasts the dog 40 days. The other, a denser food, costs $52 and lasts 47 days. Per pound, the denser food costs $1.73 and the other $1.50. Per day, the denser food costs about $1.11 and the other about $1.13, so the $52 bag costs less to feed than the $45 bag.

Sources indicate that gaps like that grow with how much your pet eats, so they matter most for big dogs. A gap of 10 cents a day comes to $36.50 a year.

To compare two dry foods this way:.

Newer labels list a cup’s weight in grams instead of kcal/kg. To get kcal/kg from those, multiply the calories per cup by 1,000 and divide by that weight. For canned food, divide your pet’s daily calories by the calories per can, then multiply by the price per can.

According to recent reports, between two sizes of the same food, every pound holds the same calories, so the lower price per pound settles it. The bigger bag’s saving depends on the food staying fresh. A veterinary nutritionist at Tufts University recommends finishing an opened bag within two to three months, so buy the size your pet empties in that time.

Switch to a new food slowly. Mix a little more of it into the old food each day for at least a week.

Scan Walmart Clearance With the App – It Can Ring Up Below the Sticker

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A Walmart clearance sticker keeps the price it was printed with, and the store may have marked the item down again since.
  • Walmart notes each store’s manager can cut prices to clear out extra stock, and that changing prices on paper tags by hand could take hours or even days.
  • Sources indicate that walmart is replacing its paper shelf tags with digital labels that show the same price the register charges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A Walmart clearance sticker keeps the price it was printed with, and the store may have marked the item down again since. Scan the item with the free Walmart app while you’re in the store. The app shows that store’s current price, and that’s what you’ll pay at the register.

Walmart notes each store’s manager can cut prices to clear out extra stock, and that changing prices on paper tags by hand could take hours or even days. The register charges the newly introduced price in the meantime.

Sources indicate that walmart is replacing its paper shelf tags with digital labels that show the same price the register charges. It said in March 2026 that it expects every U.S. store to have them within a year. A clearance sticker on the item itself is still paper, though, so it’s the likeliest place to find an old price, along with the shelf tags in any store that hasn’t switched yet.

Recent findings suggest that say a pair of kids’ sneakers carries a $14.97 clearance sticker, and the store has since cut the price to $5. The sticker still states $14.97, but the app shows $5, and $5 is what you’ll pay.

Look for clearance stickers on the displays at the ends of aisles, along the back wall of each department, and in the seasonal aisle the week after a holiday. Open the app inside the store with location sharing on, since it shows in-store prices only once it knows you’re there. Then tap the scanner icon in the search bar and scan the product’s own barcode, not one printed for shipping or storage.

The price you see applies only at that store. Walmart says prices can vary from store to store and that it doesn’t price match its own stores, so the store won’t match a lower price you found at another Walmart. Clearance is also whatever the store has left, so an item you pass up today may be gone the next time you come in.

For a major purchase you can time, like a TV or a mattress, skip the clearance hunt and wait for its category’s yearly sale season.

Scan every clearance sticker before the item goes in your cart, and buy what scans at a price you’d pay.

Download the free Walmart app and sign in before your next trip.

Used Books for a Few Dollars – Compare Prices With Shipping, Then Check Library Sales

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, before you buy a print book fresh, look for a used copy, which often costs a few dollars.
  • A hardcover that costs $30 fresh can cost $2 at a library sale or $6 with shipping from an online used-book seller.
  • According to recent reports, online, the catch is shipping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, before you buy a print book fresh, look for a used copy, which often costs a few dollars. Online, compare sellers by what you’d pay with shipping, not the listed price. Then check library book sales near you, where many books cost even less.

A hardcover that costs $30 fresh can cost $2 at a library sale or $6 with shipping from an online used-book seller. Books hold up well, so a used copy in good condition reads just like a new one.

According to recent reports, online, the catch is shipping. On a marketplace like AbeBooks, each seller sets its own shipping charge, so a $1 copy with $4 shipping costs more than a $4 copy that ships free. BookFinder.com compares offers from more than 100,000 booksellers, and its searches take shipping into account. Search the title there before you buy anywhere.

ThriftBooks, which sells millions of used books, charges nothing for standard shipping on a US order over $15, so buying several books at once can cost less than ordering them one at a time.

Locally, browse used bookstores and thrift stores, and watch for library book sales. The library’s Friends group, which raises money for the library, often runs the sale, and hardcovers commonly cost $1 to $3. Many end with a bag sale, when a full bag often costs $5 or $10. Find one on your library’s website or on Book Sale Finder, which lists library and other nonprofit book sales by state. Some libraries also keep a sale shelf or a Friends bookstore open between sales.

Before you pay, check the condition grade. ThriftBooks’ grades run from Like Fresh down to Acceptable, and AbeBooks’ guide describes a Good copy as one with average wear and every text page intact. That’s usually good enough for a book you’ll read rather than display. Ex-library copies, former library books that often carry stamps and stickers, usually cost less. To get a particular edition, search by its ISBN, the number assigned to each edition and format of a book. A hardcover and a paperback of the same title each have their own.

Trade in the books you won’t reread at a used bookstore that buys them, and ask for store credit, which is often worth at least 20% more than the cash offer.
